title: ADLS Gen2: hierarchical namespace and why it matters for analytics

videos.script: Lesson 2 renamed nothing, and for a good reason. On an ordinary storage account, a folder cannot be renamed. {{flat}} Every file in it has to be copied to a new name and deleted from the old one. For a thousand files, that is two thousand requests. {{count}} And a job that dies halfway leaves the folder in two places at once. You will watch that happen on Azurite. {{crash}} Azure's answer is one setting on the account: the hierarchical namespace. With it, the storage account becomes Data Lake Storage. {{hns}} Directories become real. A rename is one step, and each directory can carry its own permissions. {{tree}} Azurite does not have it, so you will see exactly how it refuses, and declare the real thing with Terraform instead. {{refuse}} Then the catch. The setting can be switched on, and never switched off. {{oneway}} By the end you can say which of Quitanda's two accounts gets it, and why the other one does not. {{end}}
